title: Introduction to Trigonometry: Ratios and Identities
seo_title: Introduction to Trigonometry Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: Trigonometric ratios of an acute angle of a right-angled triangle; values of the ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°; relationships between the ratios; proof and applications of the identity sin²A + cos²A = 1, only simple identities to be given (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Introduction to Trigonometry worksheet (NCERT Chapter 8): six trigonometric ratios, values of 0° to 90°, identities and finding angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.
body_html:
How it works

In a right triangle, for an acute angle A: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan A = opposite/adjacent. Their reciprocals are cosec A, sec A and cot A.

Values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, sin 60° = √3/2; cos goes the other way; tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Identities: sin² A + cos² A = 1, 1 + tan² A = sec² A, 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Example

If sin A = 3/4, find cos A and tan A.

Opposite 3, hypotenuse 4, adjacent √7

cos A = √7/4

Answer: cos A = √7/4, tan A = 3/√7

Example

Evaluate sin 60° cos 30° + sin 30° cos 60°.

(√3/2)(√3/2) + (1/2)(1/2)

3/4 + 1/4

Answer: 1

Common mistakes

  • Swapping opposite and adjacent. Look from the angle you are working with.
  • Writing sec A = 1/sin A. sec A = 1/cos A and cosec A = 1/sin A.
  • Mixing up sin 30° = 1/2 with sin 60° = √3/2.

faq.q: What are the six trigonometric ratios?
faq.a: sin, cos, tan and their reciprocals cosec, sec, cot. For angle A: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan A = opposite/adjacent.

faq.q: How do I remember the values for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°?
faq.a: sin takes the values √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2, that is 0, 1/2, 1/√2, √3/2, 1. cos takes the same values in reverse order, and tan = sin/cos.

faq.q: What are the three trigonometric identities in Class 10?
faq.a: sin²A + cos²A = 1, 1 + tan²A = sec²A (for 0° ≤ A < 90°) and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A (for 0° < A ≤ 90°).

faq.q: Can sin A be greater than 1?
faq.a: No. The hypotenuse is the longest side, so opposite/hypotenuse is at most 1.

items.q: If tan A = 12/5, find sin A (A is acute).

If tan(A + B) = √3 and sin(A − B) = 1/2, with 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B.
True or false? cot A is not defined for A = 0°.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: True. cot 0° = cos 0°/sin 0° = 1/0, which is not defined.

items.q: True or false? The value of cos θ increases as θ increases from 0° to 90°.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: False. cos goes from 1 down to 0.

items.q: Find the acute angle θ if cot θ = 1/√3.
True or false? sin θ = 4/3 for some angle θ.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: False. sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse is never greater than 1.

items.q: True or false? sin (A + B) = sin A + sin B.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: False. Take A = 60°, B = 30°: sin 90° = 1 but sin 60° + sin 30° ≠ 1.

c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: True. sec A = hypotenuse/adjacent can be greater than 1.

items.q: Find the acute angle θ if cot 2θ = √3.
True or false? cot A is the product of cot and A.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: False. cot A is one symbol: the cotangent of angle A.

items.q: If sin(A + B) = 1 and sin(A − B) = 1/2, with 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B.

items.q: True or false? cos A is the abbreviation used for the cosecant of angle A.
c: It depends on the size of the triangle
items.e: False. cos A is the cosine; the cosecant is cosec A.
